sentinel_port.description: Port on which Redis Sentinel listens for client connections.

sentinel_bind.description: IP address(es) Sentinel binds to (space-separated or `*` for all interfaces).

sentinel_dir.description: Working directory for Sentinel — used for temp files and persistence (must be writable by redis user).

sentinel_myid.description: Unique node ID. Use `auto` to let Redis generate it automatically.

master_name.description: Name used to identify this Redis master group in Sentinel.

master_ip.description: IP address of the Redis master instance.

master_port.description: Port of the Redis master instance.

quorum.description: Minimum number of Sentinels that must agree a master is down before initiating failover.

sentinel_down_after_milliseconds.description: Milliseconds to wait before marking the master as subjectively down (SDOWN).

sentinel_parallel_syncs.description: Number of replicas that can be reconfigured to replicate from the new master in parallel after a failover.

sentinel_failover_timeout.description: Maximum time (ms) allowed for a failover to complete before it is aborted.

sentinel_notification_script.description: Path to a script executed when Sentinel detects state changes (e.g., master down, failover started).

sentinel_client_reconfig_script.description: Path to a script executed after a successful failover to reconfigure clients (e.g., notify load balancers).

sentinel_replicas.description: Explicit known replica configurations (optional; usually auto-discovered).

name.description: Optional replica name (used for easier tracking).

sentinel_known_sentinels.description: Explicit known Sentinel nodes in the cluster (optional; auto-discovery recommended).

ip.description: IP address of the known Sentinel.

current_epoch.description: Current config epoch (usually omitted unless debugging).

sentinel_logfile.description: Path to the Sentinel log file. Use `-` to log to stdout.
